title: Traffic-aware Lanes: Quality Contracts & Launch Readiness for Chat/Embeddings/Rerank
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: introduce a production-grade ‘traffic-aware lanes’ capability for the hosted inference surface that routes requests into quality lanes (Gold/Silver/Bronze) based on traffic profile, cost target, and per-endpoint quality contracts. This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout checklist, and operational runbook for launch. Scope covers chat completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints in hosted mode. Motivations: reduce unit cost for low-risk workloads, maintain strict quality for high-value traffic, and provide predictable regressions protection via automated quality contracts.
business_context: Customers mixing experimental traffic with critical user flows ask for a way to limit costs without exposing core users to regressions. Platform teams want safe automated fallbacks and clear quality contracts to justify model/quantization trade-offs.
scope_in: API-level parameter: lane_hint (optional) + automatic lane assignment by telemetry
Per-endpoint quality contract definitions (chat, embeddings, rerank) with thresholded signals
Routing policy that combines latency SLO, cost budget, and quality score to assign lane
Canary rollout tooling for lane assignment changes and model swaps
Observability: lane-level dashboards, NSC (Normalized Semantic Consistency) and drift detectors
Fallback behavior and automatic rollback when quality gates fail
scope_out: Dedicated/Dedicated-managed private deployments (will be covered in a follow-up ticket)
Custom per-customer policy UIs in Console (Console hooks only, not the full UI)
New model training or fine-tuning—only model selection/variant routing
Full per-customer SLA changes—this work defines technical gates but not pricing changes
acceptance_criteria: API contract: requests accept optional lane_hint string and server returns assigned_lane in response metadata
Quality contracts defined and enforced for each endpoint: chat NSC >= 0.92 for Gold lane, embeddings pairwise similarity delta <= 0.015 for Gold, rerank NDCG drop <= 0.02 vs baseline for Gold
Latency SLOs per lane: Gold p95 <= 350ms, Silver p95 <= 600ms, Bronze p95 <= 1200ms (measured on production-like traffic)
Cost guardrail: Bronze lane must achieve >= 20% token-cost reduction vs Gold on representative workload
Canary behavior: 2 phased canaries (internal 1% traffic -> 5% customer pilot) with automated quality gate checks and explicit rollback triggers
Observability: lane-level dashboards with NSC, latency histograms, token cost, and per-prompt golden set comparisons available in Console
Alerts: automated pager when NSC drops below lane threshold for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows or when NDCG regression > threshold
No quality regression in Gold lane during a 5-day pilot against the established golden prompt set (statistical test p>0.05 for difference in NSC)
Documentation: API spec, Runbook, and Customer-facing FAQ published
E2E tests: synthetic workload test that validates assignment, fallback, and rollback behaviors in staging
design_constraints: Minimal change to existing request/response payloads; assigned_lane must be a response header or top-level metadata
Routing latency budget per request must add <5ms median overhead
Backward compatibility: requests without lane_hint must behave as today (default to previous assignment policy)
Allow operator override: support admin route to pin traffic to lane for troubleshooting
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Staging validation: deploy routing in staging with simulated traffic profiles and run full test_plan
Phase 1 - Internal canary: 1% of production traffic (internal customers) for 72 hours; automated gates must pass
Phase 2 - Pilot customers: 5% production traffic for selected pilot customers (opt-in) for 7 days; collect telemetry and feedback
Phase 3 - Gradual promotion: increase by 10% increments with 24-48 hour observation windows until 100% safe default routing enabled
Phase 4 - Post-launch: enable Console visibility and customer opt-in controls; open support playbook
test_plan: Unit tests for lane assignment logic and policy evaluation
Integration tests verifying assigned_lane is surfaced in response metadata and honored by downstream routing
Golden prompt regression tests: seeded prompts for chat/embeddings/rerank run continuously in staging and canary
Performance tests: measure routing overhead at 99th, 95th, 50th percentiles under target QPS
Chaos test: simulate model worker OOMs and validate fallback to next-best lane and automatic rollback
A/B evaluation harness: compare Gold vs candidate Gold-variant on NSC/NDCG for 7 days in canary
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quality detection false positives trigger unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: require 3 consecutive windows and multi-signal confirmation (NSC + golden-set failure + customer error rate) before rollback
Risk: Routing adds too much latency -> Mitigation: implement caching of recent assignments and pre-compute simple heuristics; fall back to default fast path if budget exceeded
Risk: Bronze lane reduces quality more than expected for adversarial prompts -> Mitigation: conservative Bronze profile, explicit exclusion lists for safety-sensitive prompt families
Risk: Alert fatigue from noisy gates -> Mitigation: combine statistical tests and smoothing to reduce false alarms and onboard SRE thresholds
